d.d: A light, brisk musical movement; a gigue.

A lively dance in 6/8 (double jig), 9/8 (slip jig) or 12/8 (single jig) time; a tune suitable for such a dance. By extension, a lively traditional tune in any of these time signatures. Unqualified, the term is usually taken to refer to a double (6/8) jig.
A dance performed by one or sometimes two individual dancers, as opposed to a dance performed by a set or team.
To move briskly, especially as a dance.
d.x: The guests were jigging around on the dance floor.

d.d: To move with a skip or rhythm; to move with vibrations or jerks.
To fish with a jig.
A double-ended vessel, generally of stainless steel or other metal, one end of which typically measures 1½ fluid ounces (approx. 44 ml), the other typically 1 fluid ounce (approx. 30 ml).
A measure of 1½ fluid ounces (approx. 44 ml) of liquor.
The sieve used in sorting or separating ore.
To alter or adjust, particularly in ways not originally intended.
d.x: You'll have to jigger it from the original specifications to get it to work.

d.d: To use a jigger.
To move, send, or drive with a jerk; to jerk; also, to drive or send over with a jerk, as a golf ball.
present participle and gerund of jig
The act of dancing a jig.
The act of using a jig; the act of separating ore with a jigger, or wire-bottomed sieve, which is moved up and down in water.
A relatively weak shaking movement; the condition or state of weakly shaking.
d.x: Give the key a jiggle and see if it opens.

d.d: Titillating depictions of scantily-clad female bodies in motion, especially in action media genres.
To shake something gently; to rattle or wiggle.
d.x: Jiggle the handle and see if the water stops.

d.d: To shake, rattle, or wiggle.
d.x: The jelly jiggled in the bowl for a few moments after it was set down.

A motion that jiggles.
That jiggles.
Something that resembles the Pokémon Jigglypuff, e.g. by being rotund, bright pink, or able to induce sleep.
Resembling or suggesting a jig.

A jigsaw puzzle.
Something that can be compared to a jigsaw puzzle.
